create.name: Buddha Eye Temple / Butsugenji
create.bio:
Buddha Eye Temple, also called Butsugenji or Buddha Eye Zen Community Temple, is a Soto Zen temple on Garfield Street in west Eugene, Oregon. Established in 2002, it is a formally registered temple of the Japanese Soto school. Its founder was Joshin Keira Roshi, a Japanese priest who trained at Sojiji and later led Shurinji in Sendai, and who died in 2023. The abbot today is his Dharma heir Ejo Patrick McMullen, ordained in 1995 and trained at Daijoji monastery in Japan, who also helps run the Soto school's North American office. Further Dharma teachers and senior students teach alongside him.

The temple keeps a monastic rhythm open to everyone: its gate opens before dawn on weekdays for zazen, chanting and an oryoki breakfast, with midday and evening services, and visitors may simply spend time in the hall or garden during the day. Tuesday and Thursday evenings add zazen and seasonal classes, and the Sunday assembly brings sitting, chanting, a Dharma talk and an introduction to meditation, with free childcare. Teachers offer sanzen and practice discussion, sesshin are held through the year, and every programme is free. Sunday talks are streamed and archived on its YouTube channel.

courses.title: Sunday Morning Assembly
courses.description: The temple's main weekly gathering: zazen with an introduction to meditation from 9 am, then chanting, a Dharma talk and community time, with childcare for young children. No registration is needed.

courses.title: Daily Schedule: weekday zazen and services
courses.description: Weekday mornings from 5 am with zazen, walking meditation, chanting and an oryoki breakfast, a midday and an evening service, and Tuesday and Thursday evening zazen followed by classes. The temple is also open during the day for quiet sitting or sutra copying.

courses.title: Sanzen and Practice Discussion with the temple's teachers
courses.description: Formal one-to-one meetings with the abbot or a lineage holder during early-morning zazen or on set afternoons, and practice discussions with the temple's Dharma teachers and elders by appointment.

free_resources.title: Dharma Talks
free_resources.description: Weekly Sunday talks from the temple, each summarised on the site and streamed and archived on its YouTube channel, from series on caring for ancestors to the Buddha's path to awakening.

free_resources.title: Jump In: getting started at Buddha Eye
free_resources.description: A newcomer's guide to the temple: the Sunday introduction to zazen, the seasonal practice schedule, working with a teacher and how to stay in touch.
